Char. eqn is

$$
\lambda^2 - 5\lambda + 6 = 0
$$

$$
\Rightarrow \lambda = 2, 3
$$

For $\lambda=2$; eigen vector is, $x_1 = \begin{pmatrix}-1\\1\end{pmatrix}$

For $\lambda=3$; eigen vector is $x_2 = \begin{pmatrix}-\tfrac{1}{2}\\1\end{pmatrix}$

Matrix $P = (x_1\ x_2) = \begin{pmatrix}-1 & -\tfrac{1}{2}\\1 & 1\end{pmatrix}$

Diagonal matrix $D = \begin{pmatrix}2 & 0\\0 & 3\end{pmatrix}$

$$
P^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix}-2 & -1\\2 & 2\end{pmatrix}
$$

Req'd diagonalization is,

$$
A = \begin{pmatrix}-1 & -\tfrac{1}{2}\\1 & 1\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}2 & 0\\0 & 3\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}-2 & -1\\2 & 2\end{pmatrix}
$$

OR

$$
A = \begin{pmatrix}-\tfrac{1}{2} & -1\\1 & 1\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}3 & 0\\0 & 2\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}2 & 2\\-2 & -1\end{pmatrix}
$$

Let $\alpha_1v_1 + \alpha_2v_2 + \alpha_3v_3 = 0$

then

$$
\begin{pmatrix}\alpha_1 + 2\alpha_2 + 2\alpha_3,\ 5\alpha_2 + 7\alpha_3,\ \alpha_1 + \alpha_2 + \alpha_3\end{pmatrix} = (0,0,0)
$$

$$
\Rightarrow \alpha_1 + 2\alpha_2 + 2\alpha_3 = 0
$$

$$
5\alpha_2 + 7\alpha_3 = 0
$$

$$
\alpha_1 + \alpha_2 + \alpha_3 = 0
$$

Determinant of the coeff. matrix

$$
= \begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 & 2\\0 & 5 & 7\\1 & 1 & 1\end{vmatrix} = 2 \neq 0
$$

$\therefore\ B$ is a linearly independent set of 3 vectors in $\mathbb{R}^3$.

Since every linearly independent set of $n$ vectors from an $n$-dimensional vector space $V$ forms a basis for $V$, we, $B$ forms a basis for $\mathbb{R}^3$.

Let $(4,5,3) = \alpha_1v_1 + \alpha_2v_2 + \alpha_3v_3$ then

$$
\alpha_1 + 2\alpha_2 + 2\alpha_3 = 4
$$

$$
5\alpha_2 + 7\alpha_3 = 5
$$

$$
\alpha_1 + \alpha_2 + \alpha_3 = 3
$$

$$
\alpha_1 = 2,\ \alpha_2 = 1,\ \alpha_3 = 0
$$

$$
\therefore\ (4,5,3) = 2v_1 + 1\cdot v_2 + 0\cdot v_3
$$

Let

$$
\alpha_1v_1 + \alpha_2v_2 + \cdots + \alpha_iv_i + \cdots + \alpha_nv_n = 0
$$

we know, $\langle 0, v_i\rangle = 0\ \forall\ i=1,2,\ldots,n$

$$
\Rightarrow \langle \alpha_1v_1 + \alpha_2v_2 + \cdots + \alpha_iv_i + \cdots + \alpha_nv_n,\ v_i\rangle = 0
$$

$$
\Rightarrow \langle \alpha_1v_1,v_i\rangle + \langle \alpha_2v_2,v_i\rangle + \cdots + \langle \alpha_iv_i,v_i\rangle + \cdots + \langle \alpha_nv_n,v_i\rangle = 0
$$

$$
\Rightarrow \alpha_1\langle v_1,v_i\rangle + \alpha_2\langle v_2,v_i\rangle + \cdots + \alpha_i\langle v_i,v_i\rangle + \cdots + \alpha_n\langle v_n,v_i\rangle = 0
$$

$$
\Rightarrow \alpha_1\cdot 0 + \alpha_2\cdot 0 + \cdots + \alpha_i\lVert v_i\rVert^2 + \cdots + \alpha_n\cdot 0 = 0
$$

$$
\Rightarrow \alpha_i\lVert v_i\rVert^2 = 0\quad \text{for } i=1,2,\ldots,n
$$

$$
\Rightarrow \alpha_i = 0\ \text{or}\ \lVert v_i\rVert^2 = 0\quad \text{for } i=1,2,\ldots,n
$$

But $\lVert v_i\rVert^2 = 0 \Rightarrow v_i = 0$, impossible;

$$
\therefore\ \alpha_i = 0\ \text{for } i=1,2,\ldots,n
$$

$$
\therefore\ \{v_1,v_2,\ldots,v_n\}\ \text{is L.I.}
$$

Step 1: Let $v_1=q_3=(0,0,1)$ then

$$

$$

Step 2:

$$
u_2=q_2-\langle q_2,u_1\rangle u_1
$$

$$
\langle q_2,u_1\rangle = 2
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

Step 3:

$$
u_3=q_1-\langle q_1,u_1\rangle u_1-\langle q_1,u_2\rangle u_2
$$

$$
\Rightarrow \langle q_1,u_1\rangle = 2,\quad \langle q_1,u_2\rangle = -1
$$

$$
\therefore\ v_3=(1,2,2)-2(0,0,1)+1(-1,0,0)=(0,2,0)
$$

$$
\therefore\ u_3=\frac{v_3}{\lVert v_3\rVert}=(0,1,0)
$$

Let $u=(x_1,y_1),\ v=(x_2,y_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2$

and $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$ then

$$
\alpha u+\beta v=(\alpha x_1+\beta x_2,\ \alpha y_1+\beta y_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2
$$

$\therefore$

$$
T(\alpha u+\beta v)=T(\alpha x_1+\beta x_2,\ \alpha y_1+\beta y_2)
$$

$$
=(2(\alpha x_1+\beta x_2)+(\alpha y_1+\beta y_2),\ 3(\alpha y_1+\beta y_2))
$$

$$
=(\alpha(2x_1+y_1)+\beta(2x_2+y_2),\ \alpha(3y_1)+\beta(3y_2))
$$

$$
=(\alpha(2x_1+y_1),\ \alpha(3y_1))+(\beta(2x_2+y_2),\ \beta(3y_2))
$$

$$
=\alpha(2x_1+y_1,\ 3y_1)+\beta(2x_2+y_2+3y_2)
$$

$$
=\alpha Tu+\beta Tv
$$

$\therefore$ $T$ is a L.I.
